payload.name: Search descriptive adjectives for habitual activity places
payload.description: When a question asks what type of place a person regularly meditates, relaxes, or practices wellness activities, and first results show only named retreats or generic memories.
content: Run an additional search combining the person's name, the activity, and descriptive location adjectives like tranquil, quiet, peaceful, nearby, or favorite.
Prefer a current habitual setting memory over a past named destination when the question implies recurring practice; use memory kind and world_start/world_end to distinguish.
Do not choose the most explicit place name; require a memory connecting the person, the activity, and a place descriptor.

solves: A literal activity+place search missed a memory describing the habitual spot as 'nearby tranquil spot' and selected a one-time retreat instead. This happens when a question asks for a regular activity's location and the correct memory uses descriptive adjectives rather than a place noun. The rule applies to wellness/leisure activities with one-time destination distractors.
